description: A hydrate that is the heptahydrate form of disodium hydrogen arsenate.
docs.label: disodium hydrogenarsenate heptahydrate

description: A hydrate of nickel sulfate containing nickel (in +2 oxidation state), sulfate and water moieties in the ratio 1:1:7.
docs.label: nickel sulfate heptahydrate

description: A hydrate that is the heptahydrate form of magnesium sulfate.
docs.label: magnesium sulfate heptahydrate

description: A hydrate that is the heptahydrate form of zinc sulfate.
docs.label: zinc sulfate heptahydrate

description: A hydrate that is the heptahydrate form of chromium trinitrate.
docs.label: chromium trinitrate heptahydrate

description: A hydrate that is the heptahydrate form of cobalt(2+) sulfate.
docs.label: cobalt(2+) sulfate heptahydrate

description: A 6-oxo steroid that is 5β-cholest-7-en-6-one substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 2, 3, 5, 11, 14, 20 and 22 respectively (the 2β,3β,5β,11α,14α,20R,22R-stereoisomer). It is a phytoecdysteroid produced by the kaladana plant Ipomoea calonyction.
docs.label: muristerone A

description: A hydrate that is the heptahydrate form of ferrous ammonium sulfate.
docs.label: ferrous ammonium sulfate heptahydrate

description: A hydrate that is the heptahydrate form of iron(2+) sulfate. It is used as a source of iron in the treatment of iron-deficiency anaemia (generally in liquid-dosage treatments; for solid-dosage treatments, the monohydrate is normally used).
docs.label: iron(2+) sulfate heptahydrate

description: A polyol marine coelenterate toxin composed of substituted N-3-hydroxypropyl-trans-3-amidoacrylamides and produced by species of Palythoa and Zoanthus soft corals (collectively called zoantharians), either as a defence mechanism or to assist them in capturing prey. An ionophore that forms cation channels through Na+/K+-ATPase, it is a potent vasoconstrictor useful in evaluation of anti-angina agents. It is considered to be one of the most poisonous non-protein substances known, second only to maitotoxin in terms of toxicity in mice.
docs.label: palytoxin

description: An organic sodium salt that is the heptahydrate form of pemetrexed disodium. Inhibits thymidylate synthase (TS), 421 dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), and glycinamide ribonucleotide formyltransferase (GARFT).
docs.label: pemetrexed disodium heptahydrate

description: A hydrate that is the heptahydrate form of sodium molybdate.
docs.label: sodium molybdate heptahydrate

description: The aglycone of protaphin, a yellow hydroxylated quinoid pigment found in aphids.
docs.label: protoaphin aglucone

description: A flavan-3,3',4,4',5,5',7-heptol that has (2R,3S,4S) configuration.
docs.label: (2R,3S,4S)-leucodelphinidin

description: A C-glycosyl compound that is the 2'-C-β-D-glucopyranosyl derivative of 1,5,8-trihydroxy-3-methoxy-7-(1',3',6',7'-tetrahydroxy-9'-oxo-4'-xanthyl)xanthone; isolated from Swertia punicea.
docs.label: swertipunicoside

description: A quassinoid that is 13,20-epoxypicras-3-ene substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 1, 6, 11, 12, 14, 15 and 21 and oxo groups at positions 2 and 16. Isolated from the ethanol extract of the stem of Brucea mollis, it exhibits cytotoxic activity.
docs.label: yadanziolide B

description: A cyclic peptide antibiotic that is A47934 lacking the O-sulfo group; it is produced by a strain of Streptomyces toyocaensis.
docs.label: A41030A

description: A flavanol that is 3,4-dihydro-2H-chromene which is substituted at positions 3, 4, 5, and 7 by hydroxy groups, and at position 2 by a 3,4,5-trihydroxyphenyl group.
docs.label: flavan-3,3',4,4',5,5',7-heptol

description: A hydrate that is the monohydrate form of iron(2+) sulfate. It is obtained from the heptahydrate by heating above 65°C. It is used as a source of iron in the treatment of iron-deficiency anaemia (generally in solid-dosage treatments; for liquid-dosage treatments, the heptahydrate is normally used).
docs.label: iron(2+) sulfate monohydrate

description: A compound of iron and sulfate in which the ratio of iron(2+) to sulfate ions is 1:1. Various hydrates occur naturally - most commonly the heptahydrate, which loses water to form the tetrahydrate at 57°C and the monohydrate at 65°C.
docs.label: iron(2+) sulfate (anhydrous)

description: A hydrate that is the heptahydrate form of hexaammonium heptamolybdate.
docs.label: hexaammonium heptamolybdate tetrahydrate
